title: Quantization profile impact assessment and threshold tuning for int8/int4 (AWQ/GPTQ)
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Objective: Produce a repeatable evaluation harness and a set of deployment gating thresholds that quantify quality regressions introduced by quantization profiles (AWQ and GPTQ) for int8 and int4 variants, and iterate on per-profile tuning knobs to meet conservative quality SLAs while maximizing cost and latency savings.

Scope: Focus on two production model families currently in the catalog (redwood-v1-like and open-instruct-13b-like). Evaluate both AWQ and GPTQ toolchains for int8 and int4 quantization. Assess: generation quality (task-specific metrics), semantic similarity, hallucination rate, and latency/cost per token. Create gating thresholds that will be used by the Console rollout automation for staged deploys.

Approach and methodology:
- Representative eval set: 2,400 prompts split across instruction-following (40%), closed-domain QA (30%), code completion (10%), math/reasoning (10%), and conversational context (10%). Prompts drawn from production telemetry samples (anonymized) + standard public benchmarks.
- Metrics: Exact Match (EM) for QA, BLEU/ROUGE for code/instructions, BERTScore and embedding cosine similarity for semantic drift, and hallucination checks via reference-based NER/slot checks. Track latency P50/P95 and cost delta per token.
- Statistical tests: paired bootstrap for metric deltas, 95% confidence intervals. Require effect sizes >0.5% (relative) to be considered meaningful for EM; for semantic metrics require >0.8% relative.
- Baseline: fp16 (or fp32 where appropriate) serving profile measured on the same hardware and runtime.
- Tuning knobs to explore: per-layer scale clipping, activation quant clipping thresholds, per-channel vs per-tensor scale, grouped quantization for attention and feedforward blocks, and selective higher-precision for normalization & layernorm.

Initial run summary (run date 2025-02-25):
- AWQ int8 (default profile): EM delta vs fp16 = -0.4% (95% CI [-0.7%, -0.1%]) on closed-domain QA; BERTScore delta = -0.5 points; latency reduction ~-20% P95; cost savings ~-18% token-level.
- GPTQ int8 (default profile): EM delta = -0.9% (95% CI [-1.4%, -0.4%]); BERTScore delta = -0.9; latency reduction ~-18%; cost savings ~-15%.
- GPTQ int4 (default profile): EM delta = -2.3% (95% CI [-3.1%, -1.5%]); BERTScore delta = -2.0; latency reduction ~-46%; cost savings ~-40%.
- AWQ int4 (default profile, experimental): EM delta = -1.8%; BERTScore -1.3; instability observed on long-context code prompts (higher hallucination rate).

Interim decision (2025-02-26):
- AWQ int8: promising. Prepare staged rollout with gating thresholds tightened via tuning.
- GPTQ int8: borderline; run knob sweeps on per-channel scales and attention-block grouping.
- int4 profiles: require additional tuning and targeted mitigations before any rollout.

Tuning actions taken (2025-02-27 to 2025-02-28):
- Enabled per-layer activation-clipping with dynamic percentile selection (empirical clipping at 99.9 -> 99.95) which reduced long-tail token errors on code prompts.
- For int4 profiles, applied selective FP16 fallback on layernorm and final LM head during inference.
- Introduced per-head quant scale for attention matrices for AWQ int4 prototype.

Post-tuning results (2025-03-01):
- AWQ int8 (tuned): EM delta = -0.25% (95% CI [-0.5%, 0.0%]); BERTScore delta = -0.3; latency -21%; cost -19%. Meets conservative acceptance criteria.
- GPTQ int8 (tuned): EM delta = -0.6% (95% CI [-1.0%, -0.2%]); still slightly above our strict EM gate but acceptable for internal beta.
- GPTQ int4 (tuned + selective FP16 fallback): EM delta = -1.4%; BERTScore -1.1; instability reduced but still failing hallucination threshold on long-context code tests.

Gating thresholds proposal for Console automated rollout:
- AWQ int8: allowed relative EM regression <= 0.5%, BERTScore drop <= 0.7, hallucination increase <= 0.5 percentage points, latency P95 reduction >= 15% required to qualify for staged rollout.
- GPTQ int8: allowed EM regression <= 1.0% for internal beta; require additional validation for public rollout.
- int4: no automated rollout until EM regression <= 1.0% and hallucination delta <= 0.8.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Telemetry and CI integration:
- Tag every eval run with quant_profile and quant_tool labels (e.g., quant_profile=awq-int8, quant_tool=awq).
- Add dashboard panels in Console: per-profile EM/BERTScore delta, hallucination rate, latency P50/P95, and sample-level diffs for failed cases.
- Build an alert that triggers when any profile exceeds gating thresholds in production sampling (sample size min 500 requests).

Risks and mitigations:
- Overfitting tuning to eval set: mitigated by splitting production telemetry samples and holding out 20% for final validation.
- Hidden failure modes in low-frequency long-context prompts: will collect 3,000 long-context samples and add targeted unit tests in the eval harness.
- Toolchain variance: AWQ and GPTQ binaries produce slightly different numerical seeds; enforce deterministic seeds and commit tuned quant artifacts to model-catalog with checksums.

Artifacts and links (see attachments): PRs, notebooks, dashboards, and raw results buckets.

Next steps (short-term):
1) Finalize gating config and add to runtime-1.21 rollout plan (owner: Marcus).
2) Run 30-day shadow sampling on 10% traffic for AWQ int8 with shadow compare enabled (owner: SRE).
3) Expand eval set diversity (owner: Research) and re-run full suite.
4) Create a long-running A/B job to surface rare failure modes and integrate into regression alerting.
acceptance_criteria: AWQ int8: relative EM regression <= 0.5% on held-out eval set and hallucination increase <= 0.5 pts
AWQ int8: latency improvement P95 >= 15% and cost per token reduction >= 15%
Int4 profiles: no automated rollout until EM regression <= 1.0% and hallucination delta <= 0.8 pts
All eval runs must be reproducible with deterministic seeds and artifacts committed to model-catalog
Dashboards and alerts created in Console for per-profile monitoring with sampling >= 500 before alerting
